title: Embedded integration pilot cheatcard (sketch)
body:
Purpose:
Quick, portable cheatcard for sellers and SEs running embedded inference pilots with customers. Not a full deck — use this during calls, hand to SE before first install, and paste into trial handoffs.

Status: rough sketch — needs engineering validation on install steps (see TODOs). Intent: 1-pager+speaker notes + quick technical checklist.

Audience:
- Platform/infra engineering leads evaluating private or dedicated inference for embedded features
- Product managers running pilot programs to validate latency, cost, and data isolation

One-line positioning to open with:
"Redwood gives you predictable, production-grade LLM inference in your environment — same controls whether hosted, dedicated, or fully private — so you can embed features without rebuilding a serving stack."

When to propose an embedded pilot (signals):
- Product needs sub-200ms p95 response in-region and has sensitive data (PII/regulatory)
- Team already has GPU capacity or is open to a small dedicated pool
- Integration timeline: 2–8 weeks, wants SLA/rollback guarantees
- Wants fine-grained cost visibility and token-level tracing

Pilot hypothesis (example):
- Cut inference unit cost by 35% vs hosted at target throughput while meeting 200ms p95 for 2k concurrent users, with logs staying in customer VPC.
- Success criteria (pick 2–3):
  - p95 latency <= 200ms for 95% of test prompts
  - Inference unit cost <= $0.003 per token at steady-state batch sizes
  - No data exfiltration events; audit logs present in customer SIEM

Quick technical checklist (must-validate during kickoff):
- Environment: customer cloud account or on-prem capacity? (AWS/GCP/Azure)
- Network: can we open egress to Redwood control plane on TCP 443? (if private, control-plane handshake plan)
- KMS/HSM integration required? Which provider and key rotation policy?
- GPU instance types available + driver stack (NVIDIA driver + CUDA version). Note: runtime supports CUDA 12+; check kernel modules.
- Expected QPS and token-length distribution (sample prompts please)
- Data residency and encryption needs (in-flight/at-rest)
- Observability hooks: can we run the tracing agent and forward to their Datadog/CloudWatch?
- Can customer provide a stable domain name and cert for mutual TLS?

Minimum pilot deliverables (what SE commits to):
- Reference deployment manifest (k8s/helm or Terraform) tailored to customer infra
- Baseline perf run (3 load shapes) + cost estimate and tuning guidance
- Security & compliance checklist and initial audit log dump
- Runbook for rollback and automated fallbacks to hosted model if local capacity fails

Tactical talking points (for discovery and demos):
- "Same API surface everywhere": engineers keep one integration while we handle model variants and routing.
- "Predictable economics": reserved capacity and quantization options to control unit costs.
- "Graceful degradation": automatic fallback to verified hosted model during capacity loss so UX doesn't break.

Common objections + short answers:
- "We can't open our network to an external control plane." -> "We support private control plane and air-gapped on-prem deployments; we can also run a lightweight agent that only initiates outbound mTLS to your control endpoint."
- "We don't have GPU ops experience." -> "We provide a turnkey Helm chart + runbook; team deploys once and our SRE/solutions engineers support the first 2 weeks of the pilot."
- "How do we avoid regression in LLM outputs?" -> "We run eval sets and can pin model versions; Redwood Optimize gives automated regression alerts tied to your prompt suites."

Pilot run plan (high level timeline):
- Week 0: Kickoff + infra checklist + access/setup
- Week 1: Deployment + smoke tests + single-node perf numbers
- Week 2: Load testing + tuning (batching, kv cache, quantization tryouts)
- Week 3: Observability + SLO verification + runbook exercise
- Week 4: Business review + recommendation (go-live, scale, or iterate)

Success handoff -> Scale recommendations (if pilot passes):
- Move to reserved capacity for predictable throughput. Propose 3-month commit aligned with estimated QPS.
- Suggested next steps: A/B test quantized vs full-precision model on 10% traffic; add prefix caching for top-10 prompt families.

Measurement templates (paste into follow-up email):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for synthetic and real traffic
- Cost: $/1M tokens broken out by model variant, batch size, and cache hit rate
- Quality: acceptance rate on N prompt evals and human rating (1–5)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm GPU types customer can provision — ask infra contact for exact instance IDs. (TODO: Ethan to own)
- Validate KMS vendor compatibility with our private control-plane flow. (TODO: Priya)
- Build short script to sample token-length distribution from their logs (PR linked above).

Speaker notes (short):
- Start with customer pain (latency/cost/controls).
- Show our fallback story early — reduces perceived risk.
- For technical decision-makers, lead with GPU/drivers and KMS. For PMs, lead with time-to-value and rollback options.

Hand-off checklist for AE -> SE before first call:
- Customer infra contact, cloud subscriptions, and support window
- Expected usage profile and sample prompt set
- Compliance constraints and required audit controls
- Any existing LLM endpoints or vendors currently used

Appendix: quick scripts & links (refs to put into Confluence page later):
- Perf harness repo: github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness
- Helm chart example: github.com/redwood-inference/charts/tree/main/embedded
- Pilot template agreement: CONFLUENCE-7152

Notes to self: keep this under 2 slides max when converted for SDR/share. This file is intentionally terse — expand into a 6-slide technical checklist only if customer asks for a formal doc.

-- end of sketch --
